question: Why did both pilot-1 supervisor controls terminate in about two milliseconds without setting memory_exceeded or timed_out?
root_cause: The monitor thread invoked /bin/ps after launching the child. The restricted command sandbox denied that process-list operation. The monitor error handler correctly killed the new process group, but the tests did not include the receipt in their assertion messages, so pilot 1 could not distinguish this fail-closed infrastructure path from a child that exited on its own.
repair: Probe the sampled-RSS backend before launching any child, identify the backend and preflight sample in every receipt, keep fail-closed monitoring after launch, split supervisor controls from transformation controls, include receipts in all assertion failures, retain raw receipts for the bound validation run, and add normal/nonzero plus child-memory and child-timeout process-group cases.
scientific_effect: None. No variant was generated and no checker was invoked while diagnosing or validating the supervisor.
